results.evidence: tests/test_actor_and_database_errors.py has one test per command. Each wraps the module's _apply so the real write runs and sqlite3.OperationalError is then raised. Each asserts exit 1, stderr == ['error: could not ...: disk I/O error'], empty stdout, and contacts and activities rows equal to the snapshots taken before the call. Because the write happens before the raise, only the rollback can leave the tables unchanged. The modules do roll back: eligibility.py:83 and hand_review.py:71 call conn.rollback(). All 5 tests in the file pass. The AC says stderr starting 'error:'; the exact-line assertion is stricter and still satisfies it.
